entities.summary: Raymond Pace Alexander was an American civil rights leader, lawyer, politician, and the first African American judge appointed to the Pennsylvania Court of Common Pleas. Born and raised in Philadelphia, he became the first black graduate of the Wharton School of Business in 1920. After graduation from Harvard Law School in 1923, Alexander became one of the leading civil rights attorneys in Philadelphia. He gained prominence as a black lawyer willing to fight for equal rights in the Berwyn desegregation case and represented black defendants in other high-profile cases, including the Trenton Six, a group of black men arrested for murder in Trenton, New Jersey.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a leading civil rights attorney in Philadelphia, Alexander played a crucial role in several landmark cases, including the Berwyn desegregation case and the Trenton Six case. His efforts helped pave the way for future generations of African American lawyers and judges, contributing to the advancement of civil rights in the United States.
